official.deadline_note: There is no single Erasmus Mundus deadline: each consortium sets its own. The EACEA catalogue states that most programmes require applications between October and January for courses commencing the following academic year.
official.application_cycle: Annual; applications for most programmes run October to January for the following academic year
official.status_note: The EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue lists 218 projects currently supported by the European Union. The catalogue is updated annually and warns that some listed programmes no longer offer scholarships because they are near the end of their funding period.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Erasmus+ Programme Guide states that selected projects 'cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders'.
benefits: Monthly scholarship of EUR 1 400 multiplied by the duration of the Master programme (12, 18 or 24 months)
No tuition fees or other mandatory participation costs may be charged to scholarship holders
The scholarship contributes to travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs
A joint degree or multiple degrees awarded by at least two institutions of the consortium
Compulsory physical mobility in at least two countries, one of which must be an EU Member State or associated country
eligibility: A bachelor's degree (first degree), or being in the last year of bachelor studies and graduating before the master's programme starts
Students from all over the world may apply, with a geographical-balance rule of no more than 10% of scholarships to one nationality
Students who have previously obtained an EMJM scholarship are not eligible for an additional scholarship under the EMJM
The scholarship is awarded only for full-time enrolment and covers the entire duration of the study programme
requirements: Apply directly to the institution running the chosen programme
Sign a Student Agreement with the consortium upon enrolment
Complete compulsory physical mobility in two countries different from the country of residence at enrolment
Demonstrate a bachelor's or officially recognised equivalent level of learning in the degree-awarding country
selection_criteria: Selection, recruitment and monitoring of individual students fall under the sole responsibility of the EMJM consortium
Scholarships are offered to the best-ranked students worldwide, with geographical balance across nationalities
coverage: Contribution to travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs, calculated as EUR 1 400 per month for the programme duration
Tuition fees and other mandatory participation costs cannot be charged to scholarship holders
application_method: Search the EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue, which can be filtered by country, duration and credits, university and field of study
Check Austria among the partner countries and open the consortium's own programme website
Apply directly to that consortium, following its own application steps and scholarship request
Contact the consortium directly for course details, application procedure and scholarship availability
official.application_route: Apply directly to the consortium running the chosen master's programme; each programme's own website holds its steps, deadlines and scholarship availability.
official.study_mode: Full-time - the scholarship is awarded for full-time enrolment and covers the entire programme duration
official.citizenship_residency: Open to students from all over the world
official.international_eligibility: Yes - students from all over the world are welcome, subject to a 10% cap per nationality on scholarships awarded
official.duration: 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits)
official.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are prestigious international master's programmes, jointly designed and delivered by a consortium of at least three higher education institutions from three different countries, including periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence. The European Commission funds scholarships for the best students, and the EACEA catalogue lists the programmes currently supported, with Austria among the filterable partner countries.
official.region: Europe and beyond - host countries are those of the consortium; Austria is one of the catalogue's partner countries
official.program_type: EU-funded joint master's scholarship (Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters, Erasmus+ Key Action 2)

not_confirmed: deadline_central - each consortium publishes its own date and no central deadline exists
english_requirement - set by each programme and its consortium
documents - published on each consortium's own application page
the specific Austrian-based consortium's intake dates and remaining scholarship places
verification.notes: The EUR 1 400 per month per scholarship holder and the rule that selected projects cannot charge tuition fees to scholarship holders are taken from the Erasmus+ Programme Guide funding rules for EMJM; the EACEA catalogue and the EC student page confirm the application route, the October to January window and worldwide eligibility.

applicant_utility.summary: This record is an umbrella, not one scholarship: pick a specific Erasmus Mundus consortium that includes an Austrian institution and apply to that consortium directly, because EACEA and the Commission take no applications. Deadlines sit with each consortium and typically fall between October and January for a September start, so your transcripts, references and language evidence have to be ready in early autumn. The money is one monthly allowance of EUR 1 400 for the whole programme, so compare it against the cost of living in each consortium city rather than the two-year total, and remember the allowance is trimmed if you spend long stretches in your own country of residence.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year bachelor's students and recent graduates with a strong grade record who want a genuinely two-country master's and can give one consortium application their full autumn.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist Austria-inclusive consortia in the EACEA catalogue and open each consortium's own scholarship page
Verify that the consortium's current funding round still offers scholarships - the catalogue warns some entries are past their funding period
Prepare an English bachelor's transcript and degree certificate, or documented proof of expected graduation
Ask referees early, as consortium letters are usually uploaded with the application rather than requested afterwards
Write the motivation letter to the consortium's published criteria instead of a generic statement
Budget visa, travel and installation costs separately, since the single allowance also has to absorb them
common_rejection_risks: Applying to the wrong body - there is no central Erasmus Mundus application form
Assuming one Europe-wide deadline and missing the consortium's own closing date
Being in the final year of a bachelor's without evidence you will graduate before the programme starts
Overlooking the compulsory mobility rule, which requires study in at least two countries and none of them your country of residence
Applying with a previous EMJM scholarship already held, which disqualifies you from a second award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Residence permits, extra health and liability insurance, and the gap between EUR 1 400 a month and living costs in the more expensive consortium cities; installation and visa costs come out of the same allowance.
document_audit: Academic records normally need certified English translations issued or verified by the degree-awarding institution
Check the consortium's scholarship document list separately from its admission list - scholarship files often add a CV, motivation letter and references
Keep proof of your last completed semester and, if asked, a residence certificate for the programme-country or partner-country classification
alerts: The 10% per-nationality cap means applicants from heavily represented countries face the tightest odds
There is one round per intake, so a missed consortium deadline usually means waiting a full year
Check each programme page for scholarship availability before investing effort, since not every catalogue entry still funds scholarships
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit online through the consortium's own portal, which handles both admission and the scholarship request; the consortium runs selection, contacts shortlisted candidates for anything extra, then issues the admission and award decision.
